title: Make vasp incar reader use first instance of each key, like vasp itself
body:
Modify vasp incar reader to use a function that only sets values in `self.params_*` if value hasn't been set before, so that first instance of each key is used, like vasp itself. 

Also clean up parsing of scalar bool values.

closes #1751

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
I am wondering how it behaves if `key` has not exist yet in `collection`.
It may be then safer to do e.g.
```python
@staticmethod
def set_if_none(d: dict[str, Any], key: str, value: Any) -> None:
    d[key] = value if d.get(key) is None else d[key]
```

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
If I recall correctly, it is appropriate to raise an error if the key is missing as this method should only be used for known keys that get instantiated with None.

Ideally the collection wouldn't be full of `None` values and this would be `setdefault`, but that is a bit much of a refactor to add to this MR.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: Clearly it'd fail, but the reader as currently implemented initializes every valid key to `None`, starting at https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/master/ase/calculators/vasp/create_input.py?ref_type=heads#L1259. I guess if it's a "non-registered" key it could be an issue, so I'll change it.
